chapter: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
title: The Rhythm Club's baby grand and the pianists who came through
summary: Only players who could really play touched the Rhythm Club's piano; Danny and Milt try to recall a classical-genius pianist, and James P. and Fats came by.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: And he opened this club, and he called it the Rhythm Club. And naturally, the musicians began to come around. And they had a piano in there, always well-tuned. It was a baby grand. And they didn't allow you to just noodle on it. You had to be able to play something, or they'd tell you, "Don't mess with that instrument. Get up from there unless you can play something." And old Joe Steele would be in there. Sammy Stewart would be in there. That other piano player...
Sammy Stewart was a piano player.
Yeah. That piano player you know. What's his name? He was kinda gay.
He worked... He had kind of bushy hair. He was a legend.
No, it's not Jerome Carrington. No, it's another one. This was another cat, a great, great musician. He's supposed to have been a Classical genius -- from Chicago he came.
He was kind of tall, and he smiled all the time. But he had a strange name. He would be in there. And James P. Johnson would come through there. Fats Waller come through there.
